verdict.rationale: FireHydrant's own docs show that an incident timeline exists: AI-drafted retrospectives 'analyze the incident's timeline' and include timelines. The Scribe captures discussions and decisions from incident bridges, and Slack `/fh update` notes are posted as updates. However, nothing explicitly documents automatic timeline capture of alerts, runbook actions and Slack chat decisions, or editing and annotating timeline entries afterward. Only retrospective fields are shown as collaboratively editable. Missing for 10: explicit docs on automatic timeline ingestion of alerts, actions and chat messages; documented post-incident editing or annotation of timeline entries; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, the incident timeline is captured automatically — alerts, actions, and chat decisions — and I can edit or annotate it afterwards

citations.quote: Analyze the incident's timeline, details, and context
the FireHydrant Scribe will be invited to your meetings to capture crucial discussions and decisions made during incident bridges
All incident notes/updates posted via Slack (`/fh update`) or via Command Center are posted to the Internal Status Page
a flexible template system, collaborative editing, and integrated incident data
